name: Haworth
assumptions: Frame MOON_ME (DE421); azimuth 0 = local north, clockwise; angles in degrees; times UTC.
No atmospheric refraction. Apparent directions use light-time and stellar-aberration correction (LT+S).
Horizon elevation includes lunar curvature; terrain beyond max_radius_m is ignored and terrain inside near_field_m is excluded (slope covers the landing zone).

Visible fractions (contract §1.1, R3-2): the horizon elevation is read at the azimuth of the body center by linear interpolation between whole-degree bins (periodic in azimuth) and treated as a straight horizontal line across the whole disc width. The visible fraction is the area of the circular segment of the disc above that line divided by the disc area (disc radius from the SPICE kernel radius and distance; the disc is approximated as a circle in the azimuth/elevation plane, ignoring the cos(elevation) compression of azimuth width). Earth counts as visible when its center is above the horizon (margin 0 deg), equivalently fraction >= 0.5.
